inline_comments.comment: This file is a developer's AI implementation prompt and was accidentally committed to the repository root. It contains no production value and exposes internal development workflow. The `.gitignore` entry added in this PR covers `.instructions/` (a directory) but NOT `instructions.md` at the root, so this file will not be automatically excluded. It must be deleted before merge.

This change inverts the logic of the non-intersection check for the second line segment, introducing a regression. The original code correctly returned `DON'T_INTERSECT` when both points p1 and p2 lie on the **same side** of line q1-q2 (`r1 !== 0 && r2 !== 0 && sameSign(r1, r2)`). The new code instead returns `DON'T_INTERSECT` only when both r1 and r2 are **approximately zero** (i.e., both points are near the line). This removes the primary early-exit guard for the same-side case: when `r1=5, r2=3` (both clearly on the same side, segments cannot intersect), the new code no longer short-circuits and proceeds to compute a spurious intersection point outside the actual segment bounds. Note that the equivalent r3/r4 check immediately above was left unchanged with the correct `!== 0` logic, making the asymmetry between the two checks obvious. This will cause incorrect edge routing in diagrams with certain geometries. Restore to: `if (r1 !== 0 && r2 !== 0 && sameSign(r1, r2)) { return; }`

This silently changes the default layout for ALL existing mindmap diagrams from `cose-bilkent` to `tidy-tree` whenever no explicit `layout:` is set in frontmatter. Tidy-tree produces a fundamentally different visual output (bidirectional horizontal tree) compared to the existing force-directed cose-bilkent layout. This is a breaking visual change for every existing mindmap embedding. The PR description lists `cose-bilkent (default)` but the code contradicts this. If tidy-tree should be the new default, this must be (a) documented as a breaking visual change, (b) bumped to a major changeset, and (c) possibly gated behind an explicit opt-in or a deprecation period. Users have no way to preserve the old behavior without editing every diagram.

`validateLayoutData` throws `'Root node is required'` when `data.rootNode` is falsy. `rootNode` is a mindmap-specific field injected by `MindmapDB.getData()` — it is not part of the standard `LayoutData` interface and will be `undefined` for every other diagram type. Since cose-bilkent is now registered as a generic layout algorithm in `render.ts` (gated by `includeLargeFeatures`), any non-mindmap diagram that specifies `layout: cose-bilkent` will throw at runtime. Remove the `rootNode` requirement from the validation or move it into a mindmap-specific pre-render check.

A large block of debug-only logging was added and left in production code. Messages prefixed with `'APA01'` (e.g., `log.debug('APA01 processing edges, count:', ...)`, `log.debug('APA01 source:', ...)`, `log.debug('APA01 elkGraph structure:', JSON.stringify(elkGraph, null, 2))`) are development artifacts that will appear at `debug` log level in production. `JSON.stringify(g, null, 2)` on a full ELK layout result can be extremely verbose. Additionally, the validation loop that iterates over all edges checking whether each source/target exists is redundant runtime overhead. Per project conventions, remove these debug traces before merge.

The `try/catch` block around `elk.layout(elkGraph)` catches the error, logs it with `log.error('APA01 ELK layout error:', error)`, then immediately re-throws. This adds no recovery logic and the `APA01` prefix signals it is temporary debug instrumentation. The catch block should either be removed (let the error propagate naturally) or replaced with a meaningful error transformation.

This entire file is dead code — it is not imported or used anywhere in the codebase. Shipping unused production modules inflates bundle size and creates maintenance burden. Either wire this up to a consuming call site or remove it from the PR.

Double-deletion of the original edge: `data4Layout.edges = data4Layout.edges.filter((edge) => edge.id !== edgeIdToRemove)` already removes the edge with `edgeIdToRemove`. The immediately following `findIndex`/`splice` block looks for `edge.id` in the already-filtered array — since the filter just removed it, `findIndex` will always return `-1` and the `splice` is unreachable. The second removal is dead code.

`_drawNodes` and `_updateNodeDimensions` are defined at the top of the file but are never called from the `draw` function (which now delegates entirely to `render(data4Layout, svg)`). `_drawNodes` only calls itself recursively and `_updateNodeDimensions` has no callers at all. Both functions are dead code. Remove them to keep the module focused.

`diagramId: 'mindmap-' + Date.now()` generates a new non-deterministic ID on every call to `getData()`. This can break any caching, diffing, or test assertions that compare layout data. Use a stable ID derived from the diagram content or a sequential counter instead.

`isGroup` was changed from `isGroup: boolean` to `isGroup?: boolean`. Because downstream code (e.g., `if (node.isGroup)` checks and `isGroup: false` discriminated-union matching in `NonClusterNode`) relies on this being required and a concrete boolean, making it optional weakens the discriminated union and could cause silent mismatches where `undefined` is treated as falsy but not the same as `false`. Keep it required or audit all consumers.

Mindmap-specific properties (`nodeId`, `level`, `descr`, `type`) were added directly to `ClusterNode` and `NonClusterNode`. These interfaces are shared across all diagram types; adding mindmap domain fields here violates separation of concerns and pollutes generic types. Per project conventions, diagram-specific type extensions belong in that diagram's own `types.ts` (e.g., `MindmapLayoutNode` already exists in `mindmapDb.ts` for exactly this purpose). Remove these fields from the generic interfaces.

Four new fields were added to `Edge`: `source?: string`, `target?: string`, `depth?: number`, and `points?: Point[]`. The `source` and `target` fields are semantic duplicates of the existing `start` and `end` fields, creating ambiguity about which to use. Callers in `cytoscape-setup.ts` already map `start`→`source` and `end`→`target` when handing off to Cytoscape. Keep a single canonical pair of fields; don't mirror them.

`let intersectionShift = 50;` is declared at the top of `executeTidyTreeLayout` but is immediately overwritten to `30` inside the `try` block (`intersectionShift = 30;`). The initial value `50` is never read. This is dead initialization; either remove the declaration-then-reassign pattern and declare `const intersectionShift = 30;` directly, or explain why 50 is a valid alternative value.

`id: \`virtual-root-${Math.random()}\`` uses a random number as a stable identifier for the virtual root node. This makes layout results non-deterministic across re-renders, complicating debugging, snapshot testing, and any caching keyed on node IDs. Use a fixed string like `'virtual-root-left'` / `'virtual-root-right'` instead.

`executeTidyTreeLayout` wraps entirely synchronous computation in `new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ... })`. There are no asynchronous operations inside the constructor callback. Use `async function` with a direct `return` (or just a regular function returning `Promise.resolve(result)`) to express intent clearly and avoid the promise constructor anti-pattern.

In `calcIntersect`, the diamond polygon points are computed using `const s = bounds.width` but the original `intersect` function used `const size = Math.max(bbox.width, bbox.height)`. For a non-square diamond node (width ≠ height), the two calculations produce different polygons. The original `max` ensures the polygon fully encloses the rendered diamond shape; using only `width` can cause edge paths to visually pierce the node boundary on taller-than-wide diamonds.

`// @ts-ignore TODO fix this (KNSV)` on the `this.calcIntersect(node as Bounds, point)` call. Per project rules, `@ts-ignore` must include an explanation of *why* the type error exists, not just a TODO. The underlying issue is that `node` is typed as `Node` (optional x/y/width/height) but `Bounds` requires them non-optional. Either assert after a guard or type the intersection function parameter more broadly.

`calcIntersect` and `intersect` both delegate to `intersect.rect`, which assumes a rectangular boundary. A `bang` shape is visually non-rectangular (it has scalloped/spiked edges), so using rectangle intersection means edge lines will appear to stop at the bounding box rather than at the shape boundary. This same issue applies to `cloud.ts`. At minimum these should document that rect-intersection is an intentional approximation.

The new "Layouts" section uses a plain ` ``` ` fenced code block instead of ` ```mermaid-example `. Per project documentation conventions, plain or ` ```md ` fences prevent the docs pipeline from rendering the diagram — users will see raw text, not a rendered mindmap. Change the fence to ` ```mermaid-example ` so the build pipeline generates both the interactive editor link and the rendered preview.

Inconsistent YAML frontmatter indentation across the `<pre>` blocks in this file. Some blocks use a single leading space (` ---`), others use four spaces (`    ---`), and some mix indentation levels within the same block. YAML frontmatter parsing is whitespace-sensitive; unexpected leading spaces before `---` delimiters can cause the parser to fail to recognize the block as frontmatter, silently rendering without the intended layout config. Normalize all frontmatter blocks to use consistent indentation (ideally no leading whitespace before `---`).

general_comments.comment: **`cose-bilkent` layout algorithm is mindmap-only despite being registered globally.** The `cose-bilkent` layout is now wired into the generic `registerDefaultLayoutLoaders()` in `render.ts` (behind `includeLargeFeatures`), making it available to any diagram type that sets `layout: cose-bilkent`. However, its `validateLayoutData` requires the mindmap-specific `rootNode` field, its render function feeds the mindmap `rootNode` through the layout pipeline, and its `cytoscape-setup.ts` treats all nodes as flat (no subgraph concept). Any non-mindmap use will either throw at validation or produce incorrect output. Either restrict this layout to mindmap only (don't register it globally) or remove the `rootNode` requirement and make the implementation genuinely generic.

**Spurious files in `cypress/platform/knsv2.html`.** The diff adds dozens of new `<pre id="diagram4" class="mermaid2">` blocks (note `mermaid2`, not `mermaid`) containing flowchart and mindmap test cases that will never be rendered by the test harness. These appear to be developer scratch/debug fixtures. Additionally, several blocks contain plain flowcharts (not mindmaps) inside `mindmap`-layout config sections. Per project conventions, scratch HTML playground files should not be committed; use a personal-username file (like the existing `cypress/platform/<username>.html` pattern) or a dedicated test spec.

**`.d.ts` declaration files added alongside `.ts` source files in the ELK package.** `packages/mermaid-layout-elk/src/render.d.ts` and `find-common-ancestor.d.ts` were added as hand-written type declarations for files that already have `.ts` source counterparts. TypeScript generates `.d.ts` files automatically during build; hand-maintaining parallel declarations creates a divergence risk (the `.d.ts` could become stale relative to the `.ts`). The `tsconfig.json` was also updated to `include` `.d.ts` files, which is non-standard. Remove the hand-written declarations and rely on the TypeScript build output.

**Changeset message is vague.** The `.changeset/hungry-guests-drive.md` message is `'feat: Update mindmap rendering to support multiple layouts, improved edge intersections, and new shapes'`. Per project rules, changeset messages should name the specific affected API or diagram type and describe the concrete behavioral change (e.g., which config option enables each new layout, what the default changed from/to). The current message does not convey that the **default mindmap layout is changing** or that `bang`/`cloud` shapes are now available as generic flowchart shapes in addition to mindmap shapes.
